A 200 g piece of copper is heated to 120°C and then placed into a calorimeter containing 200 g of water at 20°C. The specific heat capacity of copper is lower than that of water. Assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings, the final equilibrium temperature of the system will be:

  1. less than 70°C
  2. 70°C
  3. more than 70°C
  4. 120°C
